summary: Throttled finalization and 504s when requesting very large output budgets with deep prompt prefix
description: Issue summary: Customer DocuFlow AI reports repeated 504 Gateway Timeouts and stalled finalization when sending requests with ~120k token prefix and max_tokens=40k. The generation starts (initial tokens stream), throughput slows dramatically after ~30s, and the finalization step frequently times out at the load-balancer with 504. Impact: Production workflows for document summarization pause and go into retry loops causing downstream backpressure and duplicate billing events reported by the customer. Environment: Dedicated cluster (cust-dedicated-03), pinned model redwood-v1-large, autoscaling enabled but observed not to react during incidents. Occurred intermittently starting 2026-03-09 18:40 UTC and reproducible with provided prompt.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Use customer API key for cust-dedicated-03 in us-east.
3) Provide a ~120k-token prefix (customer supplied anonymized excerpt) and enable streaming=true.
4) Observe initial tokens arrive for ~20-30s, then streaming stalls; final chunk never arrives and client receives 504 from LB after ~90s.
5) Reducing max_tokens to 5k or truncating prefix to <20k tokens removes the timeout and finishes normally.

investigation_notes: Initial hypothesis: KV cache eviction thrash with very large prefix causing repeated recomputation and slow finalization.
Observed scheduler batching windows spike when per-request token budgets are extremely high; current batcher groups many oversized requests causing serialization and extended tail latency.
Autoscaler did not add nodes because node memory usage did not cross the simple threshold due to fragmentation; new instances would still not accept the fragmented memory allocations quickly enough.
Edge LB 504s appear to be after the runtime stalls in finalizer step rather than immediate OOM; logs show repeated small evictions then long compute on repeatedly rebuilt KV state.
Reproduced in staging by sending synthetic 100k token prefix and max_tokens 30k: same pattern of initial throughput then stall and 504 from LB at default timeout.

Captured heap/profile from runtime: large number of small KV allocations; GC-like pauses observed in runtime logs during finalization step (link to tar: s3://redwood-logs/sup-473201/runtime-profiles.tar.gz)
Confirmed that using a quantized model variant reduced memory pressure but did not eliminate the finalization stall when max_tokens remained very large.
Potential root cause: combination of unbounded per-request token budgets + scheduler batch policy + KV cache eviction strategy + GPU memory fragmentation.
comments: Sofia Martinez (2026-03-10): Customer provided anonymized prompt and reproduction script. Customer indicates this impacts nightly batch jobs and they are rate-limiting retries as workaround.
Daniel Park (SRE) (2026-03-10): Started reproducing in staging; observed identical scheduler batch spikes and kv eviction logs. Captured runtime profile and heap. Assigned investigation.
Lina Zhao (Serving Runtime) (2026-03-11): Confirmed runtime pauses correlate with repeated KV rebuilds. Submitted short-term patch to avoid full rebuild on eviction (PR: #rwd/serving-runtime@f2d4c1).

SRE (2026-03-11): Deployed patch to staging; staging requests with max_tokens=30k now finish but still high tail latency at scale. Need change to batcher policy and LB timeout tuning for dedicated customers.
Customer (DocuFlow AI) (2026-03-11): Applying suggested temporary mitigations (truncate prefixes to <=40k tokens, lower max_tokens). Reported immediate improvement but would like platform fix.
Support lead (2026-03-12): Opening follow-up task to audit autoscaler memory fragmentation heuristics and to add guidance to doc/limits for dedicated customers.
resolution: Workaround applied: recommended customer to trim prefix and reduce max_tokens to <=5k for immediate relief; enabled prefix chunking suggestion in their account settings. Short-term fix deployed to staging (runtime patch to avoid full KV rebuild on eviction). Next steps: modify scheduler to cap per-request batching window for oversized token budgets and tune autoscaler to consider fragmentation metrics. Plan rollout: patch to staging validated, rolling to prod for dedicated clusters in us-east starting 2026-03-13 with Canary traffic. Postmortem to follow.
